faqs.question: What's the difference between SEO and MEO?
faqs.answer: SEO focuses on ranking in Google's web search results. MEO (Map Engine Optimization) focuses on ranking in Google Maps and the local 3-pack. For businesses with physical locations, MEO often delivers faster, higher-intent traffic.

faqs.question: How long until I see results from MEO?
faqs.answer: Timing varies by market, competition, profile history, customer activity, and platform changes. We establish the agreed foundation and measurement; we do not promise a specific ranking or date.

faqs.question: Do I need to respond to every review?
faqs.answer: We handle review monitoring and response templates. Responding to reviews — especially negative ones — is one of the highest-impact MEO activities. We'll draft responses and keep your profile active.

faqs.question: Can you help if I have multiple locations?
faqs.answer: Yes, when multiple locations are included in the signed Japan Entry scope. Each eligible Google Business Profile is handled with location-specific setup, content, measurement, and review-response responsibilities.

faqs.question: What is GEO and why does it matter?
faqs.answer: GEO (Generative Engine Optimization) optimizes your content to be cited by AI search engines like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity. As more users switch to AI search, appearing in AI-generated answers is becoming as important as traditional Google rankings.

faqs.question: Do you guarantee #1 rankings?
faqs.answer: No. Search engines and AI answer systems change independently. We commit to the written implementation scope and transparent handover, not a specific ranking, citation, traffic level, or refund based on platform outcomes.

faqs.question: How is Paradigm's SEO different from other agencies?
faqs.answer: We combine traditional SEO with GEO (AI-search optimization). Most agencies still only optimize for Google. We prepare your content for ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity too — future-proofing your search presence.

faqs.question: What's included in the monthly SEO retainer?
faqs.answer: There is no separate English SEO retainer. Search-readiness work and any defined ongoing responsibilities are documented in the fixed Japan Entry scope; expanded content or integrations require written approval.

sections.title: 1. Controller and scope
sections.body: Paradigm LLC, operating paradigmjp.com from Japan, is responsible for personal data handled through this website, the Japan Entry application, related messages, and engagement operations. Current company and contact details are displayed from our site settings on the About and Legal pages.

sections.title: 2. Data we collect
sections.body: We may collect your name, company, work email, phone, website, selected modules, commercial readiness, decision authority, approval and launch timing, country or market context, message, and subsequent correspondence. We may also receive IP address, browser and device information, requested page, timestamp, referrer, and campaign parameters such as UTM values. Do not submit secrets or unnecessary sensitive information.

sections.title: 3. Why we use the data
sections.body: We use this data where reasonably necessary to:
bullets: Review Japan Entry fit, authority, timing, and launch dependencies
Respond, prepare scope and terms, deliver services, bill, support, and maintain records
Route and prioritize applications for internal operator follow-up
Protect the site, prevent spam or abuse, troubleshoot, and improve reliability
Measure aggregate page and campaign performance when analytics consent or another lawful basis applies

sections.title: 4. Systems and internal notifications
sections.body: Application records may be stored in our Supabase-backed sales systems. Operational alerts may be sent to restricted internal Slack channels and in-product operator notifications so an authorized team member can review and respond. These systems act as service providers or internal work surfaces; we do not sell application data.

sections.title: 5. Service providers, disclosure, and international processing
sections.body: We may use hosting, database, communications, security, analytics, and professional service providers under appropriate controls. Data may be processed outside your country, including outside Japan, depending on provider infrastructure. We may also disclose data when required by law, to protect rights or safety, or with your direction or consent.

sections.title: 6. Analytics, cookies, and attribution
sections.body: The site may use Google Analytics or Tag Manager, Meta Pixel, Umami, and other configured campaign-measurement tools only after optional analytics consent. Referrer and UTM campaign values may be associated with an application so we can understand its source. You may decline optional analytics in the cookie notice and change that choice at any time through Cookie settings in the footer; essential security and submission processing still operate.

sections.title: 7. Retention and security
sections.body: We use the following operational retention targets unless a longer period is required for an active engagement, accounting, dispute, security investigation, or applicable law: application and lead records are reviewed for deletion 24 months after the last interaction; analytics, attribution, and security event logs are retained for 90 days; contract, invoice, and tax records are retained for the applicable statutory accounting period. Deletion requests are handled through the privacy contact after identity verification. We use access controls and other reasonable safeguards, but no internet transmission or storage system can be guaranteed completely secure.

sections.title: 8. Your rights and choices
sections.body: Subject to applicable law, you may request access, correction, deletion, restriction, objection, or portability, and may withdraw consent where processing relies on consent. We may need to verify identity and may retain records where law or overriding obligations require it. You may also complain to an applicable data-protection authority.

sections.title: 9. Automated support and prioritization
sections.body: The website may use AI-assisted chat and internal rules to summarize or prioritize information. These tools support human operations; a form submission does not automatically accept or reject a contract, and material engagement decisions are confirmed by an authorized person.

sections.body: We may update this policy and will publish the revised date on this page. For privacy requests or questions, contact:

items.a: The setup fee is fixed at $12,000 USD. The standard monthly service is included at no additional monthly charge for the first six months, then $995 per month from month seven. Third-party fees and approved work outside the fixed scope are separate.

items.q: What is included in the fixed setup?
items.a: The package covers the agreed localized revenue-site launch, Japan trust and compliance coordination, a local discovery foundation, an eligible inquiry or payment-routing path, bilingual support setup, analytics baseline, and handover materials. The exact deliverables are confirmed before work starts.

Company incorporation, tax or legal opinions, regulated licences, inventory, logistics charges, advertising spend, payment-provider fees, third-party software, photography, and work outside the agreed launch scope are not included unless added in writing.

items.q: Is launch guaranteed in 21 business days?
items.a: It is a launch target, not an unconditional guarantee. It assumes complete source materials, required account access, a single empowered approver, prompt feedback, and no external compliance or provider delay. We identify blockers before kickoff.

items.q: Who is the package designed for?
items.a: It is designed for established SMBs in Europe, North America, and Australia that can make a fast owner-led or executive decision. Sector and headcount are less important than decision speed, a real offer, and the ability to supply launch inputs.

items.q: Do we need a Japanese entity, bank account, or Japanese-speaking employee?
items.a: Not for every launch. The required structure depends on what you sell and how payment, fulfilment, support, and regulated obligations apply. We coordinate the launch path but do not replace legal, tax, banking, or licensed professional advice.

items.q: Can we cancel the ongoing service?
items.a: The setup engagement remains governed by the agreed scope. The standard monthly service is included at no additional monthly charge for the first six months. From month seven it is $995 per month and may be cancelled for future periods under the signed service terms; fees already earned and third-party commitments are not reversed.

We review fit, authority, timeline, source context, and launch constraints. A submitted application is not acceptance of an engagement. If the package fits, we confirm scope, dependencies, terms, and the start date before work begins.

faq.heading: Questions foreign founders ask
faq.q1: Do I need a Japanese legal entity to start?
faq.a1: Not for every launch. The required structure depends on your offer, payment, fulfilment, support, tax, and regulated obligations. We coordinate implementation but do not replace legal or tax advice.
faq.q2: How do payments work without a Japanese bank?
faq.a2: The eligible inquiry or payment-routing path depends on provider acceptance, your entity and settlement setup, product type, and compliance requirements. Provider fees and approvals are separate.
faq.q3: How long until I'm live in Japan?
faq.a3: The package uses a 21-business-day target after kickoff, complete inputs, required access, and the agreed approval path. External reviews or scope changes can move the date.
faq.q4: Do I need to speak or write Japanese?
faq.a4: No. Everything with you is in English. All Japanese-facing work — site, support, compliance — is handled on our side.
faq.a5: $12,000 one-time setup, with the standard monthly service included for the first six months, then $995/month from month seven. Third-party costs and approved out-of-scope work are separate.
faq.q6: Can't I just use Google Translate or DeepL for my site?
faq.a6: Machine translation can help with words but does not decide information architecture, buyer context, required disclosures, provider constraints, trust signals, escalation, or ownership. The package addresses the agreed launch system, not translation alone.
faq.q7: How is Paradigm different from hiring my own Japanese team?
faq.a7: Hiring builds internal capability; the package is a fixed external launch scope. Choose based on control, timing, existing team capacity, and the responsibilities you need to retain internally.
faq.q8: What happens after the engagement ends? Will I be left on my own?
faq.a8: The agreed handover materials and ownership are documented in scope. The standard monthly service is included for six months, then $995/month unless cancelled under the signed terms.

finalCta.heading: Stop leaving Japan on the table.

comparison.heading: The difference between "translating" and actually entering Japan
comparison.sub: Most options leave you with a translated site that still doesn't convert. Paradigm is Japan operations — not just words.
comparison.item1Body: Translation alone does not define buyer context, required disclosures, routing, analytics, provider dependencies, support, or ownership.
comparison.item2Body: Language barrier, opaque pricing, and waterfall processes built for domestic clients. You'll spend weeks in email translation hell before seeing a single deliverable.
comparison.item3Body: Translation ≠ localization ≠ market entry. You need payments, compliance, discovery, and support — not just words on a page.
comparison.item4Body: An internal hire and a fixed launch package solve different needs. The package is designed for a fast external launch scope with documented handover.
